'''Derrick Bernard Favors''' (born July 15, 1991 in [[Atlanta]], [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]]) is an [[United States|American]] [[basketball]] player. He is a 6' 10" power forward. He most recently played for [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]]. 

==High school==
Favors, from [[South Atlanta High School]], was ranked as one of the best high school basketball players in the class of 2009. [[Scout.com]] rated him the #1 player in the country<ref>[http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&pid=88&yr=2009 Favors #1 by Scout]</ref>, #2 in the [[ESPNU]]100<ref>[http://insider.espn.go.com/ncb/recruiting/tracker/espnu100?&action=login&appRedirect=http%3a%2f%2finsider.espn.go.com%2fncb%2frecruiting%2ftracker%2fespnu100 Favors #2 by ESPNU]</ref>, and #4 by [[Rivals.com]]. On March 14, 2009, he led South Atlanta to the Georgia Class AAA state championship. He scored 38 points and had 21 rebounds in the championship game against [[Westover High School]].<ref>[http://insider.espn.go.com/ncb/recruiting/tracker/player?page=onthetrail&recruitId=43657&action=login&appRedirect=http%3a%2f%2finsider.espn.go.com%2fncb%2frecruiting%2ftracker%2fplayer%3fpage%3donthetrail%26recruitId%3d43657 Derrick Favors caps career in style]</ref> He was named to the 2009 [[McDonald's All-American Team]]. He led the East to a 113–110 victory and was named the [[MVP]] of the game. He scored 19 points and had 8 rebounds.<ref>[http://sports.espn.go.com/highschool/rise/basketball/boys/news/story?id=4035376 Favors Named MVP of McDonalds All American Game].</ref> Favors was selected to participate in the 2009 [[Nike Hoop Summit]] in [[Portland, Oregon]] but pulled out due to personal reasons<ref>[http://www.draftexpress.com/article/Nike-Hoop-Summit-International-Rosters-Announced-3145/ Derrick Favors Pulls Out of Nike Hoop Summit]</ref> and he was also selected to play in the 2009 [[Jordan Brand Classic]] at [[Madison Square Garden]] where he scored a game-high 21 points and was named [[MVP]] for the black team, while [[Renardo Sidney]] was named MVP for the white team.<ref>[http://sports.espn.go.com/highschool/rise/basketball/boys/news/story?id=4080678 Big men shine in [[Jordan Brand Classic]]</ref>
He finished his senior season averaging 28.1 points, 13.3 rebounds, 5.0 blocks, 3.0 steals and 2.0 assists per game and holds the career records in points (2,341), rebounds (1,511) and blocked shots (741).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ramblinwreck.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/favors_derrick00.html|title=Derrick Favors Player Bio}}</ref>

==College==
Favors committed to [[Georgia Institute of Technology|Georgia Tech]] in January 2009, which he chose over [[University of Georgia|Georgia]], [[University of Memphis|Memphis]], and [[North Carolina State University|North Carolina State]].

Favors played both power forward and center for [[Paul Hewitt]]'s Yellow Jackets. The front court consisted of a three man rotation of Favors, [[Gani Lawal]] and [[Zach Peacock]]. In ACC games, he averaged 11.8 points and 8.7 rebounds per game and shot 62.5% from the field. He also helped lead the Yellow Jackets to the ACC tournament finals against [[Duke]]. During the tournament, he posted 17 points, 9.8 rebounds and 3 blocks per game.

==NBA==
On April 9, 2010, Derrick Favors announced he would forgo his final three years of college eligibility to enter the [[2010 NBA Draft]].<ref>[http://community.foxsports.com/goodmanonfox/blog/2010/04/09/georgia_techs_favors_to_declare,_sign_with_agent Favors Going Pro]</ref>
